memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: It is to be with him, and he is to read it all the days of his life so that he may learn to revere the Lord his God and follow carefully all the words of this law and these decrees and not consider himself better than his fellow Israelites and turn from the law to the right or to the left. Then he and his descendants will reign a long time over his kingdom in Israel. - Deut 17:19b-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells us the goal of the king's daily reading of Scripture, that he would not consider himself better than his fellow Israelites and would not turn from God's commands. Power tempts people to look down on others and to think the rules no longer apply to them. God's Word was meant to keep the king humble, grounded, and obedient.

What a picture of true leadership. The greatest man in the nation was to see himself as a brother among his people, not a superior above them. His authority did not make him better; it made him more accountable. Humility, not arrogance, was to mark God's king.

This runs completely against the way the world thinks about power, yet it is exactly how Jesus led. Though He was Lord of all, He took the form of a servant, washed His disciples' feet, and did not count Himself too high to serve (Phil 2:5-7). The path to lasting honour in God's kingdom is downward, through humility and service. Whatever measure of influence God has given you, over children, colleagues, or a congregation, He calls you to hold it with humility, never looking down on others. Where might God be inviting you to lead through humble service rather than pride?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where does authority tempt you to look down on others?
2. How does Jesus redefine what true leadership looks like?
3. What would humble, servant-hearted leadership look like for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me humble in whatever influence You give me. Let me lead and serve like Jesus, never thinking myself better than others. Amen.
